title: The Envelope Under the Door
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] For the better part of a year, on the first of every month, I've slipped an envelope of cash under the door of the family renting the unit below mine.
Narrator: Their situation isn't a secret exactly, everyone on the floor knows the father's been out of steady work since the factory downsized, but nobody talks about it.
Narrator: [carefully] I started small, an amount that wouldn't be missed from my budget, uncertain whether it would even help or go unnoticed among their bills.
Narrator: What mattered to me was that it arrived without a name, so receiving it wouldn't cost them anything in dignity, the way a direct offer sometimes does.
Narrator: [reflective] Last week, the wife knocked on my door holding the envelope, and I nearly panicked before realizing she wasn't accusing me of anything.
Narrator: She'd worked out, through elimination, that my schedule was the only one matching the timing.
Narrator: [honestly] She didn't ask me to confirm it; she just stood there, eyes wet, saying she wanted whoever it was to know how much it had meant.
Narrator: I could have denied it, but lying to her face felt like a smaller betrayal than being found out, and a betrayal nonetheless.
Narrator: [gently] Since then, things have been slightly awkward between us, an occasional nod that carries more weight than it used to.
Narrator: I worry that being known might change why I keep doing it, that some quiet corner of my intention could start performing for an audience of one.
Narrator: [calmly] So this month, I asked her not to mention it to anyone, and I've started varying the day I leave it, hoping to blur the pattern again.
Narrator: Whether that's overthinking a simple kindness, I couldn't say, but I'd rather guard it too carefully than let it drift into something I'm secretly proud of.
Narrator: [encouraging] The envelope still goes under the door every month, known or not, because the reason I started never depended on anyone noticing in the first place.

quiz.question: What has the narrator been doing every month for about a year?
options: Slipping an envelope of cash under their door
Inviting the downstairs family to dinner
Lending them his car
Writing them letters
quiz.explanation: On the first of every month, he slips an envelope of cash under the door of the family renting the unit below his.

quiz.question: Why did he keep the gift anonymous?
options: He was embarrassed by the small amount
So receiving it wouldn't cost them anything in dignity, unlike a direct offer
He wanted to surprise them on a birthday
It was against building rules
quiz.explanation: He wanted it to arrive without a name attached so that receiving it wouldn't cost them any dignity.

quiz.question: How did the wife figure out it was him?
options: He accidentally told her
She found his handwriting on a note
Through a process of elimination based on whose schedule matched the timing
A neighbor told her directly
quiz.explanation: She worked it out through a process of elimination involving every neighbor on the floor, based on matching schedules.

quiz.question: What did the narrator do when she confronted him?
options: He denied it completely
He told her the truth rather than deny it
He moved out
He asked her to pay him back
quiz.explanation: Although tempted to deny it, he told her the truth because lying to her face felt like a smaller but still real betrayal.

quiz.question: What is he doing now to protect his intention?
options: He asked her not to tell anyone and started varying the day he leaves the envelope
He stopped giving the money entirely
He asks for a receipt each time
He now gives the money in public
quiz.explanation: He asked her not to mention it to anyone else and started varying the day, hoping to blur the pattern again.

quiz.question: How had the narrator supported the neighbouring family for about a year?
options: My guest tonight drives for a ride-hailing app
I usually just say I got up for water, which isn't exactly a lie
The director praised the onboarding redesign in front of the whole department this morning
He anonymously placed a cash envelope beneath their door each month.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: He anonymously placed a cash envelope beneath their door each month.

quiz.question: What allowed the wife to identify the likely donor?
options: A passenger left a bag on the back seat after a short trip
She wakes to pray while the rest of the household sleeps
His schedule matched the timing of the envelope deliveries.
Dimas isn't even around to see the email
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: His schedule matched the timing of the envelope deliveries.

quiz.question: Why does he admit the truth instead of denying her suspicion?
options: First, that money wasn't earned by me
During a stretch of insomnia two years ago
If nobody corrects it, this becomes the version of events everyone quietly accepts
A lie would add another betrayal to a well-meant gift.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: A lie would add another betrayal to a well-meant gift.

quiz.question: How does he try to restore some anonymity afterward?
options: He insisted, practically forced a portion into my hands
That she mention the habit in their study group to motivate other women
He varies the delivery day and asks her to keep silent.
You did plenty of work refining it
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: He varies the delivery day and asks her to keep silent.

quiz.question: What principle guides his continued monthly giving?
options: A generous way to close out our conversation
The family's need matters more than whether his kindness is noticed.
She worried sharing it would hollow out something that currently feels entirely hers
I'll just reply privately to the director, thank her
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: The family's need matters more than whether his kindness is noticed.
